content.text:
I submitted **index 4** (Nb 0.456, V 0.544) as the best composition. At 8.56e-6 A, it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured.

| Index | Nb fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.714 | -3.17e-6 A |
| 11 | 0.505 | 6.26e-6 A |
| 4 | 0.456 | 8.56e-6 A |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose as the vanadium content increased. Index 4 is the most V-rich composition in the library, so there was nothing further in that direction to test.
- **First measurement:** I started at the Nb-rich end because MEGNet predicted a 2.70 eV band gap for Nb₉V₂O₂₅. That is below the 3.22 eV illumination, so it should absorb. The measurement came back negative.
- **Model support for the result:** MEGNet also predicts that the V-rich phases absorb at this energy (NbV₂O₇ at 2.36 eV, NbVO₄ at 1.47 eV). In contrast, NbVO₅ (3.48 eV) is predicted not to.

**Limitations:**
- With only three merit measurements, 13 of the 16 compositions were never tested. The model's uncertainty on the untested middle compositions (Nb about 0.52–0.60, e.g. indices 2, 6, 8, 9) was large enough that one of them could beat index 4.
- I used none of the five XRD measurements, so I never checked which crystal phases are actually present in the films.
